hazard_consequence_node.label: HazardConsequence
hazard_consequence_node.name: VCE
hazard_consequence_node.evidence: "The explosion was fueled by vapor released from a 2000-gallon tank of highly flammable liquid."
hazard_consequence_node.explanation: The primary hazardous consequence is a vapor cloud explosion: flammable solvent vapors were generated from an overheated unsealed process tank, accumulated in the building, and ignited, producing the destructive overpressure that is the main focus of the investigation. The subsequent long-duration fire was a secondary consequence.

entity_nodes.label: Material
entity_nodes.name: heptane, isopropyl alcohol, and normal propyl alcohol
entity_nodes.evidence: a more than 2000-gallon liquid mixture of heptane, isopropyl alcohol, and normal propyl alcohol
entity_nodes.explanation: These flammable solvents were charged to mix tank 3, heated, vaporized, and their vapors fueled the explosion.

entity_nodes.label: Location
entity_nodes.name: mix tank 3
entity_nodes.evidence: a 2000-gallon ink vehicle batch containing more than 10,000 pounds of flammable liquid in mix tank 3
entity_nodes.explanation: Mix tank 3 was the process vessel where the solvent mixture was heated and from which vapor was released.

entity_nodes.label: Location
entity_nodes.name: production area of the CAI/Arnel building
entity_nodes.evidence: accumulate in the building production area
entity_nodes.explanation: The solvent vapor accumulated and mixed in this enclosed building area before ignition.

condition_nodes.label: Phase
condition_nodes.name: Vapor
condition_nodes.evidence: released enough heptane/alcohol vapor into the unventilated building to fuel the explosion
condition_nodes.explanation: The hazardous material was present as a flammable vapor cloud at the time of the explosion.

condition_nodes.label: Temperature
condition_nodes.name: High temperature
condition_nodes.evidence: most likely caused the flammable liquid to overheat
condition_nodes.explanation: Uncontrolled steam heating raised the solvent mixture temperature until it boiled and generated vapor.

condition_nodes.label: Volatility
condition_nodes.name: High volatility
condition_nodes.evidence: forms a low-boiling (positive) azeotrope with an average boiling point of 165.6°F
condition_nodes.explanation: The low-boiling solvent mixture readily vaporized when heated, promoting vapor cloud formation.

condition_nodes.label: Combustibility
condition_nodes.name: Combustible
condition_nodes.evidence: CAI heated Class I flammable liquids in unsealed tanks inside a closed building
condition_nodes.explanation: The solvent mixture was flammable and capable of supporting ignition and explosion.

condition_nodes.label: ReleaseType
condition_nodes.name: Continuous release
condition_nodes.evidence: As long as the steam valve was open, the boiling mixture would continue to release many hundreds of pounds of flammable vapor
condition_nodes.explanation: The vapor release occurred over hours while the steam valve remained open and the mixture boiled.

condition_nodes.label: Confinement
condition_nodes.name: High confinement
condition_nodes.evidence: the vapor cloud accumulated and was confined inside the closed CAI/Arnel building
condition_nodes.explanation: The closed building, together with ventilation being turned off, allowed flammable vapor to remain confined/retained in the production area and increased explosion severity.

condition_nodes.label: Dispersion
condition_nodes.name: Dispersed
condition_nodes.evidence: thoroughly mix the heptane and alcohol vapor throughout the production area
condition_nodes.explanation: The released vapor dispersed through the production area and formed a near-homogeneous flammable mixture.

event_nodes.label: InitiatingEvent
event_nodes.name: Steam valve on mix tank 3 left open, allowing the flammable mixture to boil
event_nodes.evidence: the mix tank 3 heater steam valve was left open, allowing the flammable mixture to boil in the unsealed tank
event_nodes.explanation: Leaving the steam valve open initiated the abnormal overheating and vapor generation sequence.

event_nodes.label: IgnitionSource
event_nodes.name: Unknown ignition source
event_nodes.evidence: An unknown ignition source ignited the flammable atmosphere, causing the explosion
event_nodes.explanation: The report confirms ignition occurred, but the exact ignition source could not be identified.

event_nodes.label: InitiatingEvent
event_nodes.name: Building ventilation fans turned off while flammable liquid heating remained active
event_nodes.evidence: Shortly before 6:00 pm, the last CAI employee in the building turned off the dust collector fans, wall-mounted exhaust fans, and fresh air supply fan, then locked the building and left for the night.
event_nodes.explanation: The incident report explicitly identifies ventilation shutdown / inadequate ventilation as a causal contributor to vapor accumulation in the building, but the current graph does not represent this step.
